message.content:
Can a metric space be complete exactly when every nested sequence of nonempty closed sets with diameters tending to 0 has a common point?

If the nested-set property holds, take a Cauchy sequence (x_n), let F_n be the closure of its n-tail, observe that (F_n) satisfies the hypotheses, and use the property to obtain x in the intersection, where x_n → x because d(x_n,x) ≤ diam F_n → 0.

If M is complete and (F_n) satisfies the hypotheses, choose x_n ∈ F_n, note that (x_n) is Cauchy because d(x_m,x_n) ≤ diam F_n for m>n, let x_n → x, and use closedness to place x in every F_n.
